claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,n), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x: the batched parallel Pollard-rho algorithm with distinguished points and the full secp256k1 automorphism group (order 6) in proof.md succeeds with probability at least 0.49 using at most 2^129.2032 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, P=2^20 parallel walks with Montgomery-batched affine additions (realizing the reference price by explicit construction), per-step orbit canonicalization (itemized at 1.1 units), cycle-escape checks (0.1 units), table operations and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^136 bytes deterministically (worst-case, no pruning); preprocessing is at most 2^30 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. This score is transparently worse than the BSGS baseline (129.000802); it is submitted as a corrected, defensible accounting of the rho+automorphism approach per the v1 review, not as a leaderboard improvement. Heuristics: standard Pollard-rho random-walk model on the automorphism quotient (Teske, van Oorschot-Wiener, Bos et al.); 1-/2-cycle escape rule with charged checks, longer fruitless cycles heuristically negligible; distinguished-collision (1+epsilon) overhead absorbed in the Markov 2x budget; collision coefficients usable with overwhelming probability; Montgomery batching efficiency (textbook). All disclosed in proof.md.

experiments.purpose: Check Pollard-rho scalar recovery (with negation-map orbit reduction, coefficient tracking through the automorphism, and collision solving) on a small additive cyclic group. This does not establish production curve behavior, the GLV automorphism, batched affine additions, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: secp256k1-ecdlp: Pollard rho with order-6 automorphisms, honest accounting (v2)
